properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/12/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8180425
Permit API: 125-22753
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/12/2024
Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/10/2023 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/10/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 991387
Permit API: 015-23733
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/10/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's (Blackhill) Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/10/2023 at 1525 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted to evaluate remedial activities that were conducted after a release that occurred on 4/6/2023.Moody and Associates Inc. (Moody's)(Environmental consultant) was onsite during my inspection and have been conducting field screenings for Blackhill. Since the release that occurred on 4/6/2023, Blackhill has had the entire southern stormwater conveyance channel excavated (photos #2, 3 and 4). Blackhill reported that soil readings in the channel were now field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Excavation points on both sides of the access road culvert are now acting as sumps for the collection of residual fluids. A water truck was stationed at these points today, recovering any collected fluids. The pad surface area that was determined to be impacted by the release has been excavated as much as possible (photos #6 and 7). Blackhill explained that collected fluids shown in photo #7 are also being recovered. Fluid in this area, which is located right next to the initial release point, was field measured at ~17.8mS/cm today. Blackhill reported that equipment will be brought in on either 4/11/2023 or 4/12/2023 to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure in order to excavate beneath them. The impacted stormwater basin has been emptied to where just a few puddles remain (photo #1). All water collected from the basin was stored in tanks shown in photo #9 and continues to be trucked offsite for disposal or reuse. I field measured a small puddle near the stormwater channel entry point of the basin which returned a reading of ~1.75mS/cm. All impacted materials that have been recovered are stored in lined and covered waste containers which are held on secondary containment (photo #8). All violations associated with the releases from 1/2/2023 and from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1620 hours.As a follow-up to the violations cited on 4/6/2023, the DEP requests a summary of the quantity of fluids collected in regards to the produced water release, including the stormwater basin, and where the water was transported after collection. This information can be provided in the NOV response.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8261421
Permit API: 015-22301
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/13/2026
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Blackhill Energy's Kline B well pad located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 1/13/2026 at 0815 hours. The weather was 28 degrees F with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #394552 is tied to the release in CTS.On 1/12/2026, Blackhill Energy reported to the DEP that approximately 1 barrel (42 gallons) of produced fluid was discovered to have been released to the pad surface at ~0730 hours. The release occurred after condensed fluids within the low pressure pipeline were pressurized and were able to escape through a 2" connected pipe (photo #1). Blackhill reported the release within 2 hours of discovery and began remediation as soon as possible. During remediation on 1/12/2026, scraping of the impacted material and recovery of fluids was mainly superficial due to the pad materials being frozen. Throughout the remediation process, temperatures rose, thawing some of the pad material and requiring a couple locations of deeper excavation. Impacted materials were placed within 2 lined residual waste containers onsite (photo #5). During my inspection, pad materials within the impacted areas were field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings ranging from 0.1 to 2.2mS/cm. Fluids located closest to the impacted area were field measured for electrical conductivity below 1.0mS/cm. The DEP recommends continuing screening and recovery of any impacted materials and collecting characterization samples to confirm that cleanup is complete. Based on the reported release of ~1 barrel of produced fluids to the pad surface, outside of secondary containment, violations of the following are cited against API #015-22301 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S 691.402(b)I departed the site at 0945 hours.

Comments: On 03/13/19 DEP Soil Scientist Ed Bates was conducting an inspection to evaluate Act 2 compliance at the Siegel well site, due to a prior oil based mud spill. Bates observed the OBM impacted soil on secondary containment, but noted impacted soil had spilled, the impacted soil was no longer appropriately covered, and the secondary containment was insufficient. Bates contacted this WQS to inform me of violations observed at the site. I contacted Curtis Small of Chevron to inform him of Bates' observations and that I was going to be conducting an inspection shortly. Small indicated he would also head to the site. At approximately 1225 hours I, along with Water Quality Specialist Supervisor John Carson, conducted an inspection of the site. Oil & Gas Inspector James Braunns was also present at the site conducting an inspection prior to the fluid rig coming onto the site. The impacted soil stockpile appeared to have been covered with tarps, but was now largely exposed. Spilled impacted soil was observed and the secondary containment lacked berms on two sides of the pile. WQSS Carson and I also noted mild accelerated erosion in the channel to the basin. It is recommended the channel be addressed to prevent further erosion. The well tags appeared to have been completed, but the writing had faded and was no longer legible. Toward the conclusion of the inspection Curtis Small of Chevron arrived on site. We discussed our observations with Small, who indicated the impacted soil had been approved for disposal and disposal was planned for the following week. Small indicated the spilled material would be removed and confirmatory samples collected. Small also indicated the well tags would be addressed to ensure they were legible.

In the on site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan with all required components and a Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan. The access road to the well site was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site all appeared to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed along the road or the perimeters of the well site.The Department traveled to the area of the well pad where the release was previously observed, no holes filled with diesel fluid were observed and no petroleum-based odor was detected in this area. The Department observed production equipment within secondary containment adjacent to the previous spill area, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production equipment. Production tanks were also observed to be in secondary containment and no fluid leak or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near these tanks. An above ground storage tank (AST) was observed on site and within a secondary containment, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank. The 14H wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it that has the well's name and permit number on it, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead.Violations issued during IR 3923540 shall remain outstanding at this time as a Notice of Intent to Remediate or a Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

Comments: Samuel Louderback (DEP Geoscientist) and I took electrical conductivity (EC) readings from pooled liquid and soil of the pad surface, which ranged from 0.60-7.7 mS/cm. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Violations for an apparent brine release will remain open. The DEP recommends removal of pooled liquid with relatively high (>1.0 mS/cm) EC from the pad surface, wheelie trailer containment, and the NE basin. Air temp 44F JLP

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 11/08/2023
Comments: On 11/08/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well. The following was observed:Operator and well information on site (Photos 1, 2). I recommend placing the rest of the well information on the same sign that has the operator information.Pumpjack in motion upon arrival, some grease/oil on gravel. I recommend removal (Photo 3). Wellhead, production equipment were in generally good condition (Photos 2-5). Mild corrosion. Additional equipment adjacent to the well approximately 40 feet away - there is a depression around the equipment and it is filled with water; dead vegetation around depression, no high conductivity reading. I recommend addressing the depression and exploring the cause of the depression and dead vegetation - unclear if cause if from equipment or pooled water (Photos 6).Downslope of the well were five production tanks within an earthen berm. The berm was in generally good condition, however the pooled water within the berm contained high conductivity readings, specifically in front of tank 1. The sediment within the berm had adequate readings, however the rest of the pooled water had slightly elevated readings. A slightly elevated conductivity reading was taken within the gravel/sediment below the valve of tank 5. This area was relatively small and is recommended that any affected material is removed and disposed of properly. A corroded piece of equipment noted near tank 5 (Photos 7-22, see captions for specific locations). I notified the operator while onsite; a vac truck later was there removing the fluid as I was leaving. Plans are to add equipment to catch fluids when the vac truck removes the hose from the valves. It is noted that the access road has multiple uses, including agricultural, however the access roads to the well sites require routine monitoring and maintenance.Due to the observation of elevated conductivity readings within the pooled water and prompt remediation, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being noted and were immediately corrected. A follow up inspection to ensure there is not residual production fluids within the berm. No additional violations are being issued right now, however additional violations may be forthcoming.

Comments: Onsite for an incident response to a reported release from the operator. The release was reported on 5/15/2020 at 13:45pm. The delay of site investigation/response was due to restrictions based upon the COVID 19 pandemic. The release occurred as a result of a 210bbl steel tank failure and it appears that the bottom of the tank had developed a hole and or multiple holes. It was reported that 30bbls was lost from the tank directly to the earthen dike substrate. The earthen dike area is designed in a manner with two levels, the oil tanks are located at a higher elevation than the brine storage tanks. Crude oil was observed seeping out of the rock substrate inside the dike down-gradient from the oil tanks. A small sump was dug to collect the oil and pumped into a poly tank. At the time of the inspection there is no visual indication that the oil has migrated outside of the earthen dike footprint/substrate. The department has requested that the operator remove the 210bbl steel tank and remove the impacted material. As well as recover as much oil as possible. At this time a formal written plan will not be required unless site conditions change or cleanup actions are not conducted in a timely manner. Violations are noted

Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources was onsite and said STL Resources plans to continue the investigation of the extent of this spill area once the containment has been removed. The top layer of soil has been removed in this area adjacent to the containment in about a 10 ft. x 10 ft. area. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of thewell pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being hauled off site or pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in the northwest stormwater vault. In the southwest stormwater vault, the conductivity of the water was 1,939 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.3 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 23.7 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 71.9 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 133.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32 uS/cm. Seep 3 was not able to be screened with the conductivity meter due to the lack of water at the seep. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 90.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.6 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, 3445592, and 3467217.

Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-015 collected on 8/10/2022 at 14:00 as part of inspection report #3405181 at the Repsol Johnson (02-135) Well Site. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-015 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Barium - 122 ug/L; Strontium- 7.21 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- 4,900 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 904.1 mg/L. (Photo 1)Repsol submitted a 15 day response to NOV #406500 on August 30, 2022. According to the response letter, Resource Environmental was engaged to conduct site characterization work for an unknown volume of 'suspected produced water' spilled to the stormwater, soils, and gravels of the Johnson Pad. On August 11, 2022, Resource Environmental conducted screening surveys of stormwater pools and measured Electrical Conductivity readings of between 1.61 and 7.14 mS/cm on the pad surface. Additional characterization took place on August 12, 2022 through the collection of soil samples. Resource Environmental will conduct followup screenings and further site delineation is scheduled for September 6, 2022 following the removal of mobile tanks from the impacted area. Violations noted.

Comments: On May 14, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4179087, 4179852, 4179896, and 4179921.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance.I left the site at 1400 hours.

Annuli gas checks were performed starting at ~ 10:40. Eric used a MSA Altair 5X multi gas detector that was calibrated on 8/12/20, Selman confirmed gas show.- There was remedial work done on the 2H, 4H and 6H wells at the end of 2017. See photo #3 for post remedial work WBDs. Also attaching .pdf to Insp. Report.Ending PBUT pressures and gas screenings are listed below: (* indicates a gas sample was collected).
